label: Group aggregate — Dialogue Acts filtered bar (all speakers)
description: Bar chart of the dialogue-act mix pooled across every session in the group, limited to act types above 5% of the pooled corpus. Each bar is an act category's count; taller bars show which act types dominate. This is the audited pooled act mix, not a per-session average.

label: Group aggregate — Sentiment compound by session
description: One bar per transcript in the group showing that session's mean compound sentiment (-1 most negative to +1 most positive). Compare bar heights to see which sessions skewed positive or negative overall. One value per session, not a within-session timeline.

label: Group aggregate — Total words by session
description: One bar per transcript in the group showing the total words spoken in that session. Use it to compare session length and verbosity across the group. One value per session.

label: Group aggregate — Acts over time (cross-session overlay)
description: Dialogue-act activity over time with each session drawn as its own line on a shared session-relative minute axis (not one wall-clock timeline). Compare the shape of act usage across sessions; the x-axis is minutes from each session's own start.

label: Group aggregate — Sentiment cross-session overlay
description: Sentiment trajectory for each session overlaid on a shared session-relative minute axis. Each line is one session's compound sentiment over its own elapsed time; use it to compare emotional arcs across sessions rather than absolute clock time.

label: Group aggregate — Pauses cross-session overlay
description: Pause activity for each session overlaid on a shared session-relative minute axis. Each line tracks one session's pausing over its own elapsed time; compare where silences cluster across sessions.

label: Group aggregate — Emotion cross-session overlay
description: Emotion intensity for each session overlaid on a shared session-relative minute axis. Each line is one session's emotion signal over its own elapsed time; compare emotional dynamics across sessions, not absolute clock time.

label: Group aggregate — Prosody RMS cross-session overlay
description: Prosodic energy (RMS loudness) for each session overlaid on a shared session-relative minute axis. Each line tracks one session's loudness over its own elapsed time. Gallery-only by default; requires voice/prosody features.

label: Group aggregate — Sentiment compound across sessions (per speaker)
description: Bars comparing the same canonical speaker's mean compound sentiment across the group's sessions. Use it to see whether a given person trends more positive or negative from session to session. Speakers are matched by canonical identity across transcripts.

label: Group aggregate — Stats word count across sessions (per speaker)
description: Bars comparing the same canonical speaker's word count across the group's sessions. Shows how one person's verbosity changes session to session. Speakers matched by canonical identity across transcripts.

label: Group aggregate — Stats segment count across sessions (per speaker)
description: Bars comparing the same canonical speaker's number of speaking turns (segments) across the group's sessions. Shows how often one person took the floor in each session. Speakers matched by canonical identity.

label: Multispeaker Sentiment Over Time
description: Sentiment over time with one line per speaker on a shared timeline. The y-axis is compound sentiment (-1 negative to +1 positive); use it to see how each speaker's tone rises and falls and where speakers diverge.

label: Rolling Sentiment (Per Speaker)
description: Rolling (smoothed) compound sentiment for a single speaker over the conversation. Smoothing reduces turn-to-turn noise so you can see that speaker's sustained mood trend. One chart per speaker.

label: Emotion Profile – All Speakers
description: Bar chart of emotion-category intensities aggregated over all speakers. Each bar is an emotion; taller bars mean that emotion is more present overall.

label: Emotion Profile (Per Speaker)
description: Bar chart of emotion-category intensities for a single speaker. Each bar is an emotion; compare heights across speakers to see who expresses which emotions most. One chart per speaker.

label: Emotion Radar (Polar) – Global
description: Polar radar of all-speaker emotion intensities. Each axis is an emotion category and distance from the center is overall intensity; a quick visual fingerprint of the conversation's emotional balance.

label: Emotion Radar (Polar) – Per Speaker
description: Polar emotion radar for a single speaker. Each axis is an emotion and distance from the center is that speaker's intensity for it. One chart per speaker.

label: Contextual Emotion Label Counts
description: Bar chart of segment-level contextual emotion labels across the whole transcript (experimental classifier, distinct from lexical emotion). Each bar is one softmax label (anger, disgust, fear, joy, neutral, sadness, surprise); taller bars mean that label was assigned more often.

label: Contextual Emotion Label Counts (Per Speaker)
description: Bar chart of contextual emotion labels for a single speaker (experimental classifier, distinct from lexical emotion). Each bar is one softmax label; compare heights across speakers to see who was labeled with which emotions most. One chart per named speaker.

label: Fine-grained Native Label Prevalence
description: Bar chart of the most frequent fine-grained emotion labels across the transcript (experimental multilabel classifier, distinct from lexical and contextual emotion). Each bar is a native label (for example approval, disapproval, or gratitude); taller bars mean that label fired more often. Shows up to the top 15 labels by prevalence.

label: Fine-grained Native Label Prevalence (Per Speaker)
description: Bar chart of the most frequent fine-grained emotion labels for a single speaker (experimental multilabel classifier). Each bar is a native label; taller bars mean that label fired more often for that speaker. Shows up to the top 15 labels by prevalence. One chart per named speaker.

label: Contextual Emotion Label Counts (Excluding Neutral)
description: Bar chart of segment-level contextual emotion labels across the transcript with the neutral label omitted. Each bar is an absolute assignment count for a non-neutral softmax label; use this when the inclusive label-count chart is dominated by neutral.

label: Contextual Emotion Label Counts Excluding Neutral (Per Speaker)
description: Per-speaker bar chart of contextual emotion labels with neutral omitted. Each bar is an absolute assignment count for a non-neutral softmax label. One chart per named speaker with at least one non-neutral label.

label: Contextual Emotion Share of Non-Neutral
description: Bar chart of each non-neutral contextual emotion label as a share of all non-neutral assignments across the transcript (neutral omitted). Shares use the full non-neutral total as denominator and sum to 1 when non-empty.

label: Contextual Emotion Share of Non-Neutral (Per Speaker)
description: Per-speaker bar chart of each non-neutral contextual emotion label as a share of that speaker's non-neutral assignments (neutral omitted). Shares use the speaker's full non-neutral total and sum to 1 when non-empty. One chart per named speaker with at least one non-neutral label.

label: Fine-grained Prevalence Excluding Neutral
description: Bar chart of the most frequent fine-grained emotion labels across the transcript with neutral omitted before ranking. Each bar is an absolute prevalence count; shows up to the top 15 non-neutral labels. Use this when the inclusive prevalence chart is dominated by neutral.

label: Fine-grained Prevalence Excluding Neutral (Per Speaker)
description: Per-speaker bar chart of the most frequent fine-grained emotion labels with neutral omitted before ranking. Each bar is an absolute prevalence count; shows up to the top 15 non-neutral labels. One chart per named speaker with at least one non-neutral label.

label: Fine-grained Share of Non-Neutral
description: Bar chart of each displayed non-neutral fine-grained label as a share of all non-neutral prevalence across the transcript (neutral omitted). The denominator is the full non-neutral total before top-15 truncation, so when more than 15 non-neutral labels are present the displayed bars may sum to less than 1. Categories match the excluding-neutral count chart.

label: Fine-grained Share of Non-Neutral (Per Speaker)
description: Per-speaker bar chart of each displayed non-neutral fine-grained label as a share of that speaker's full non-neutral prevalence (neutral omitted). The denominator includes non-displayed non-neutral labels, so when more than 15 non-neutral labels are present the displayed bars may sum to less than 1. Categories match the excluding-neutral count chart. One chart per named speaker with at least one non-neutral label.

label: Entity Types – Global
description: Counts of named-entity types (people, places, organizations, dates, etc.) across the whole transcript. Taller bars mean that entity type was mentioned more often.

label: Entity Types (Per Speaker)
description: Counts of named-entity types for a single speaker. Shows which kinds of entities each person references most. One chart per speaker.

label: Locations Map – Global
description: Map of location entities mentioned in the transcript, geocoded where possible. Markers show places referenced across all speakers; use it to see the conversation's geographic footprint. Ambiguous place names may be omitted.

label: Locations Map (Per Speaker)
description: Map of location entities mentioned by a single speaker, geocoded where possible. Markers show the places that person referenced. One map per speaker.

label: Speaker Interaction Timeline
description: Timeline of speaking turns across the conversation, with each speaker on its own track. Shows turn-taking order, who spoke when, and turn lengths along the time axis.

label: Speaker Interaction Timeline (Per Speaker)
description: Speaking-turn timeline focused on a single speaker, showing when that person held the floor across the conversation. One chart per speaker.

label: Speaker Interaction Heatmap
description: Heatmap of who interacts with whom. Rows and columns are speakers; cell intensity is the combined count of responses and interruptions from row speaker to column speaker. Darker cells mean more frequent exchanges.

label: Speaker Interaction Matrices
description: Matrix of speaker-to-speaker interaction counts. Rows and columns are speakers and each cell's color intensity shows how often one followed or addressed the other; darker cells mean more interaction.

label: Dominance Analysis
description: Dominance score per speaker: (interactions initiated minus interactions received) divided by total interactions, counting both interruptions and responses (actor→target roles). The y-axis runs from -1 (mostly received) to +1 (mostly initiated). Taller positive bars mark speakers who drove more exchanges.

label: Speaking Floor Share
description: Per-speaker speaking-time floor share from valid segment durations (claimed speaking time; overlaps not collapsed). Rendered when total valid duration is positive, even if the floor equity index abstains.

label: Turn-taking Equity Summary
description: Session turn-taking equity indices on a 0–1 axis. Floor equity and response-latency fairness: higher is fairer. Interruption inequity: higher is more asymmetric; interruption balance (1 − inequity) is presentation-only.

label: Speaker Interaction Network (Graph)
description: Graph-layout view of the speaker interaction network. Nodes are speakers and edge weight reflects the strength of exchanges; use it to spot central speakers and isolated participants.

label: Interruption Matrix
description: Matrix of interruptions between speakers. Each cell shows how often the row speaker interrupted the column speaker; darker cells mean more interruptions in that direction.

label: Response Matrix
description: Matrix of responses between speakers. Each cell shows how often the row speaker responded to the column speaker; darker cells mean more frequent responses in that direction.

label: Momentum Over Time
description: Conversational momentum per time window (60s windows, 30s step). The y-axis is a weighted index that adds lexical novelty and turn-taking energy and subtracts pause rate, repetition rate, and loop rate. Higher values mean more new content and active exchange; dips mark stalls.

label: Engagement Time Series
description: Engagement score (0-1) per time window. The score is a weighted, normalized combination of segment count, average segment length, and question count in each window. Higher values mark the most active stretches; the x-axis is elapsed time.

label: Speaking Rate Time Series
description: Speaking rate over time in words per minute (total words in each window divided by window length, scaled to a minute). Higher values mean faster speech; use it to spot rushed or slow passages across the conversation.

label: Sentiment Time Series
description: Overall sentiment over time for the whole conversation. The y-axis is compound sentiment (-1 to +1); track rises and falls to see the conversation's emotional arc.

label: Conversation Phase Durations
description: Bar chart of how long each detected conversation phase lasted (opening, main, closing). Bar height is duration in seconds; compare heights to see which phase dominated the conversation.

label: Temporal Dynamics Dashboard (Turn Frequency & Segments)
description: Dashboard combining turn frequency and segment activity over time. Use it to see how turn-taking density evolves across the conversation.

label: Temporal Dynamics – Speaking Rate
description: Dashboard view of speaking rate over time. Higher values mean faster delivery; use it to compare pace across phases of the conversation.

label: Q&A Timeline
description: Timeline of question-and-answer exchanges. Markers show where questions are asked and answered along the conversation; use it to see the rhythm of Q&A.

label: Response Quality Distribution
description: Histogram of answer quality scores (0-1) across matched question-and-answer pairs. The x-axis bins the overall score (a weighted blend of directness, completeness, relevance, and length); the y-axis counts answers per bin. A right-shifted shape means generally higher-scored answers.

label: Question Type Breakdown
description: Breakdown of question types (such as open versus closed, factual versus probing). Each slice or bar is a type's share of all questions asked.

label: Response Time Analysis
description: Distribution of response times between a question and its answer. Longer times suggest hesitation or complex answers; use it to spot slow exchanges.

label: Verbal Tics (Per Speaker)
description: Counts of verbal tics and filler words (um, like, you know, etc.) for a single speaker. Taller bars mean that filler is used more by that speaker. One chart per speaker.

label: Entity Sentiment Heatmap
description: Heatmap of sentiment expressed toward entities. Rows are entities and color shows the tone directed at each (positive versus negative); use it to see which topics or people are discussed warmly or critically.

label: Entity Sentiment by Type
description: Sentiment grouped by entity type (people, places, organizations, etc.). Bars show average tone toward each category; compare to see which kinds of entities draw positive or negative sentiment.

label: Entity Mentions (Per Speaker)
description: Entities mentioned by a single speaker with the sentiment attached to each. Shows what that person talks about and how positively or negatively. One chart per speaker.

label: Emotional Contagion Matrix
description: Matrix of emotional contagion between speakers. Each cell measures how strongly a shift in the row speaker's expressed emotion is followed by a shift in the column speaker's; darker cells mean a stronger directed association from row to column. This reflects temporal association, not proven causal influence.

label: Echo Network Heatmap
description: Heatmap of language echoes where speakers reuse each other's words or phrases. Darker cells mean one speaker echoed another more; use it to spot alignment or mirroring.

label: Echo Timeline
description: Timeline of echo events where speakers repeat each other's language. Markers show when echoes occur across the conversation; clusters indicate stretches of strong mirroring.

label: Pause Duration Histogram
description: Histogram of pause durations across the conversation. The x-axis is pause length and bars count how many pauses fall in each bin; a long tail indicates frequent long silences.

label: Pause Timeline
description: Timeline of pauses across the conversation. Markers and heights show where silences occur and how long they last; clusters reveal hesitant or reflective stretches.

label: Moments Timeline
description: Timeline of notable moments detected in the conversation (such as emotional peaks or shifts). Markers show when each moment occurs; use it to jump to highlights.

label: Speaker Repetition Frequency
description: How often each speaker repeats their own earlier content, by frequency. Taller bars mean more self-repetition; useful for spotting emphasis or circling back.

label: Cross-Speaker Interaction Types
description: Counts of cross-speaker exchanges by model-assigned interaction type (agreement, disagreement, and related labels) inferred from semantic similarity. Each bar is the number of exchanges placed in that category. These are automatic classifications and may be noisy, not a verified measure of consensus.

label: Similarity Distribution
description: Distribution of semantic-similarity scores between utterances. The x-axis is similarity (0 unrelated to 1 near-identical); a mass at high values indicates lots of repetition or shared content.

label: Repetitions by Speaker
description: Count of repeated content per speaker. Taller bars mean that speaker reiterated points more often across the conversation.

label: Repetition Classification
description: Classification of detected repetitions (such as self versus cross-speaker, paraphrase versus verbatim). Each bar is a category's share of all repetitions.

label: Average Similarity by Speaker
description: Average semantic similarity of each speaker to the rest of the conversation. Higher bars mean that speaker's contributions were more aligned with others' content.

label: Agreement/Disagreement Breakdown
description: Counts of cross-speaker exchanges the model labelled as agreement versus disagreement, inferred from semantic similarity. Bars compare how many exchanges fell into each label. These are automatic classifications and may be noisy, not a direct measure of consensus.

label: Speaker Repetition Frequency (v2)
description: How often each speaker repeats their own earlier content (v2 embedding-based engine). Taller bars mean more self-repetition.

label: Agreement/Disagreement Breakdown (v2)
description: Counts of cross-speaker exchanges the model labelled as agreement versus disagreement (v2 embedding-based engine). Bars compare the label counts. These are automatic classifications and may be noisy, not a direct measure of consensus.

label: Similarity Distribution (v2)
description: Distribution of semantic-similarity scores between utterances (v2 embedding-based engine). The x-axis is similarity (0 unrelated to 1 near-identical); high mass indicates repeated or shared content.

label: Repetitions by Speaker (v2)
description: Count of repeated content per speaker (v2 embedding-based engine). Taller bars mean more reiteration by that speaker.

label: Repetition Classification (v2)
description: Classification of detected repetitions by type (v2 embedding-based engine). Each bar is a category's share of all repetitions.

label: Average Similarity by Speaker (v2)
description: Average semantic similarity of each speaker to the rest of the conversation (v2 embedding-based engine). Higher bars mean more alignment with others' content.

label: Topic Modeling Diagnostics
description: Diagnostic plots for the topic model (such as coherence or fit by number of topics). Use them to judge model quality and how many topics are well supported when interpreting the other topic charts.

label: Discourse Analysis
description: Four-panel view of topics across discourse phases (opening, main discussion, and closing, split by position in the conversation): topic prevalence and average topic confidence as phase-by-topic heatmaps, plus per-phase segment counts with topic diversity and average confidence. Use it to see how topics shift between phases.

label: LDA Topic-Word Heatmap
description: Heatmap of word weights per LDA topic. Rows are topics and columns are top words; darker cells mean that word is more characteristic of that topic. Use it to interpret what each topic is about.

label: NMF Topic-Word Heatmap
description: Heatmap of word weights per NMF topic. Rows are topics and columns are top words; darker cells mean that word is more characteristic of that topic (NMF as an alternative to LDA).

label: Topic Evolution Timeline
description: How topic prevalence changes over the course of the conversation. Each line or band is a topic; rising values show where that topic gains attention along the timeline.

label: Speaker-Topic Engagement Heatmap
description: Heatmap of how much each speaker engages with each topic. Rows are speakers and columns are topics; darker cells mean that speaker contributed more to that topic.

label: Expected Topic Proportions
description: Overall expected share of each topic across the conversation. Bars show each topic's prevalence; taller bars are the dominant themes.

label: Topic Distribution (Per Speaker)
description: Topic distribution for a single speaker. Bars show how that person's contributions split across topics. One chart per speaker.

label: Dialogue Acts – Filtered Bar (Per Speaker)
description: Bar chart of dialogue-act counts for a single speaker, limited to act types above 5% of that speaker's utterances. Each bar is an act type; taller bars mean that act is used more. One chart per speaker.

label: Dialogue Acts – Bar (Per Speaker)
description: Bar chart of dialogue-act counts for a single speaker. Taller bars mean that act type (question, statement, etc.) is used more by that speaker. One chart per speaker.

label: Dialogue Acts – Global Filtered Bar
description: Bar chart of dialogue-act counts across all speakers, limited to act types above 5% of all utterances. Each bar is an act type; taller bars mean that act occurs more overall.

label: Dialogue Acts – Global Bar
description: Bar chart of dialogue-act counts across all speakers. Taller bars mean that act type occurs more across the whole conversation.

label: Dialogue Acts Over Time – All Speakers
description: Dialogue-act usage over time across all speakers. The x-axis is time; lines or bands show how act types rise and fall through the conversation.

label: Dialogue Acts Over Time (Per Speaker)
description: Dialogue-act usage over time for a single speaker. Shows how that person's act mix changes through the conversation. One chart per speaker.

label: Conversation Loop Network
description: Network of recurring conversational loops (repeated act and response patterns). Nodes and edges show which exchange patterns cycle; denser links mean stronger looping behavior.

label: Conversation Loop Timeline
description: Timeline of detected conversation loops. Markers show when repeating interaction patterns occur; clusters indicate stretches where the conversation circled.

label: Conversation Loop Act Patterns
description: Common dialogue-act sequences that form conversational loops. Bars show how frequent each act pattern is; use it to see the conversation's habitual exchange structures.

label: Pauses Distribution (Voice) – Global
description: Distribution of pause durations measured from the audio across all speakers. The x-axis is pause length; the shape shows how silences are spread. Requires voice/acoustic features.

label: Pauses Distribution (Voice) – Per Speaker
description: Distribution of pause durations measured from the audio for a single speaker. Shows that person's silence patterns. One chart per speaker; requires voice features.

label: Pauses Timeline (Voice)
description: Timeline of pauses detected from the audio. Markers show where and how long silences occur across the conversation. Requires voice features.

label: Hesitation Map
description: Scatter of speech segments by speech rate (x, words per second) against pause count (y), measured from the audio. Points toward the upper-left combine slower speech with more pauses. It shows where speech slows and pauses cluster; it does not measure uncertainty. Requires voice features.

label: Burstiness (Per Speaker)
description: Burstiness of a single speaker's speech, that is how clustered versus evenly spaced their talking is. Higher values mean speech comes in bursts. One chart per speaker; requires voice features.

label: Rhythm Comparison
description: Comparison of speech rhythm across speakers. Bars or curves contrast timing regularity; use it to see who speaks more steadily versus erratically. Requires voice features.

label: Rhythm Scatter
description: Scatter of speakers by speech rate (x, words per second) against rhythmic variability (y, nPVI of voiced runs). Each point is a speaker; it contrasts how fast versus how evenly each speaker talks. Requires voice features.

label: F0 Contours (Per Speaker)
description: Pitch (F0) contours over time for a single speaker. Shows how intonation rises and falls; use it to read expressiveness or monotone delivery. One chart per speaker; requires voice features.

label: F0 Slope Distribution
description: Distribution of pitch (F0) slopes across the conversation. Rising versus falling slopes indicate intonation patterns (for example questions versus statements). Requires voice features.

label: Prosody Profile Distribution (Per Speaker)
description: Distribution of prosodic profile features for a single speaker. Shows the spread of that speaker's loudness, pitch, and rhythm measures. One chart per speaker; requires prosody features.

label: Prosody Profile Correlation (Per Speaker)
description: Correlation between prosodic features for a single speaker. Highlights which acoustic measures move together for that person. One chart per speaker; requires prosody features.

label: Prosody Timeline
description: Prosodic features over time across the conversation. Tracks loudness and pitch dynamics along the timeline. Requires prosody features.

label: Prosody Compare Speakers
description: Box plots comparing prosodic features across speakers. Each box shows the spread of a feature for a speaker; use it to see who is louder, higher-pitched, and so on. Requires prosody features.

label: Prosody Fingerprint Scatter
description: Scatter placing speakers by their prosodic fingerprint. Each point is a speaker; nearby points have similar voices. Requires prosody features.

label: Prosody eGeMAPS Distribution (Per Speaker)
description: Distribution of eGeMAPS acoustic descriptors (a standardized voice feature set) for a single speaker. Shows the spread of those measures for that speaker. One chart per speaker; requires prosody features.

label: Prosody Quality Scatter
description: Scatter of speech segments by harmonics-to-noise ratio (x, HNR in dB) against loudness (y, RMS in dB), colored by speaker. Lower-HNR points may indicate noisier or breathier audio. Requires prosody features.

label: Voice Tension Curve
description: Acoustic strain over time, computed from voice features (energy, pitch range, and speech rate) and smoothed. The y-axis is a unitless tension index; higher values mean more acoustic strain in the signal. This measures the acoustic signal, not psychological stress. Requires voice features.

label: Sentiment vs Arousal (Mismatch)
description: Scatter comparing text sentiment (x, VADER compound) against measured vocal arousal (y, an acoustic proxy from energy, pitch range, and rate). Each point is an utterance; points far from the trend show where words and voice diverge. It surfaces divergences only and does not infer intent.

label: Voice Mismatch Timeline
description: Timeline of moments where text sentiment and measured vocal arousal diverge. Markers flag where the words and the voice signal disagree (the mismatch score on the y-axis); use it to locate divergences for review. It does not detect sarcasm, intent, or suppressed emotion.

label: Voice Drift Timeline (Per Speaker)
description: How a single speaker's voice fingerprint moves away from their session baseline over time (the drift score on the y-axis). Higher values mean the measured voice is further from baseline. It reports the measured change only, without attributing a cause. One chart per speaker; requires voice features.

label: Flesch Reading Ease (All Speakers)
description: Flesch Reading Ease score per speaker. Higher scores mean easier-to-follow speech; lower scores indicate denser, more complex language. Bars compare speakers.

label: Readability Indices (All Speakers)
description: Several readability indices per speaker (such as Flesch-Kincaid grade level). Compare bars to see whose language is more complex; higher grade-level metrics mean harder to follow.

label: Structural Features (All Speakers)
description: Structural language features per speaker (such as sentence length and clause use). Bars compare how each speaker structures their speech.

label: Word Count (All Speakers)
description: Total word count per speaker. Taller bars mean that speaker said more; a quick measure of who talked most.

label: Lexical Diversity — TTR (All Speakers)
description: Type-token ratio (TTR) per speaker. Higher values mean more unique words relative to total words, but TTR is length-sensitive.

label: Lexical Diversity — MTLD (All Speakers)
description: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD) per speaker. Omits speakers with too few tokens for a stable estimate.

label: Lexical Diversity — Hapax Rate (All Speakers)
description: Share of word types that appear only once (hapax legomena) per speaker.

label: Word Cloud (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most frequent words, with stopwords removed. Larger words were said more often by that speaker. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the most frequent words across all speakers, with stopwords removed. Larger words appear more often in the conversation.

label: Word Cloud Bigrams (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most frequent two-word phrases (bigrams). Larger phrases were used more by that speaker. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud Bigrams – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the most frequent two-word phrases (bigrams) across all speakers. Larger phrases occur more in the conversation.

label: Word Cloud TF-IDF (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most distinctive words by TF-IDF, which highlights words characteristic of that speaker rather than merely frequent. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud TF-IDF – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the conversation's most distinctive words by TF-IDF, emphasizing terms that stand out rather than merely common ones.

label: Word Cloud TF-IDF Bigrams (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most distinctive two-word phrases by TF-IDF. Highlights characteristic phrases for that speaker. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud TF-IDF Bigrams – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the conversation's most distinctive two-word phrases by TF-IDF. Emphasizes standout phrases over merely common ones.

label: Word Cloud Tics (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's verbal tics and filler words. Larger items are used more by that speaker. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud Nouns (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most frequent nouns. Larger nouns were said more often; highlights what that speaker talks about. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud Nouns – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the most frequent nouns across all speakers. Larger nouns appear more; highlights the conversation's subjects.

label: Word Cloud Verbs (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most frequent verbs. Larger verbs were used more; highlights that speaker's actions and processes. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud Verbs – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the most frequent verbs across all speakers. Larger verbs appear more; highlights the conversation's actions.

label: Word Cloud Adjectives (Per Speaker)
description: Word cloud of a single speaker's most frequent adjectives. Larger adjectives were used more; highlights that speaker's descriptive language. One cloud per speaker.

label: Word Cloud Adjectives – All Speakers
description: Word cloud of the most frequent adjectives across all speakers. Larger adjectives appear more; highlights the conversation's descriptive tone.

label: Group pooled — NER entity types (full corpus)
description: Counts of named-entity types (people, places, organizations, etc.) pooled across the whole group corpus. Taller bars mean that entity type appears more across all sessions combined; a corpus-level view, not per session.

label: Group pooled — NER top entities
description: Most frequently mentioned named entities across the entire group corpus. Bar length is total mentions pooled over all sessions; use it to find the people, places, or organizations the group talks about most.

label: Group pooled — entity sentiment top entities
description: Top entities across the group corpus alongside the sentiment expressed toward them. Reads as which entities are discussed most and whether the surrounding tone is positive or negative, pooled across all sessions.

label: Group pooled — topic prevalence (group LDA)
description: Prevalence of each topic from a single topic model fit over the pooled group corpus. Bars show each topic's share of discussion across all sessions combined; corpus-level topics, not per-session.

label: Group pooled — topic prevalence (group BERTopic)
description: Prevalence of each topic from a group-level BERTopic refit over pooled source segments (not joined transcript topic IDs). Empty or all-outlier fits emit no chart.

label: Group pooled — mean emotion profile
description: Mean emotion profile across the whole group corpus. Each bar is the average intensity of an emotion category pooled over all sessions; use it for the group's overall emotional fingerprint.

label: Group pooled — tic counts (full corpus)
description: Counts of verbal tics and filler patterns pooled across the entire group corpus. Taller bars mean that tic occurs more across all sessions combined.

label: Group pooled — corpus totals
description: Corpus-level totals (such as words, segments, and speakers) summed across every session in the group. A single combined summary of the whole group rather than per-session bars.

label: Group pooled — interactions interruptions initiated
description: Interruptions started, pooled across the group corpus and attributed to each speaker. Taller bars mean that speaker interrupted others more often across all sessions combined.

label: Group pooled — interactions interruptions received
description: Interruptions received, pooled across the group corpus per speaker. Taller bars mean that speaker was interrupted more often across all sessions combined.

label: Group pooled — contagion top directed edges
description: Strongest directed emotional-contagion links pooled across the group corpus. Each edge reads as 'a shift in speaker B's emotion tends to follow speaker A'; longer bars mean a stronger association aggregated over all sessions. Reflects association, not proven causal influence.

label: Polite Tension Index (Per Speaker)
description: Polite tension index per speaker (plus a Global bar), a derived score combining positive-vs-negative affect mismatch, trust-neutral signals, emotion entropy, and volatility. Taller bars suggest more outwardly polite speech layered over underlying tension. It is a heuristic composite, not a measure of intent or sincerity.

label: Suppressed Conflict Score (Per Speaker)
description: Suppressed conflict score per speaker (plus a Global bar), a derived index flagging where neutral or positive wording coexists with signs of strain. Taller bars point to speakers whose words may understate disagreement. It is a heuristic and does not confirm hidden conflict.

label: Institutional Tone vs Affect Delta (Per Speaker)
description: Gap between an institutional or formal speaking tone and the underlying measured affect, per speaker (plus a Global bar). Larger bars mean a wider divergence between how formal the language sounds and the affect signals beneath it. It is a derived heuristic, not a judgement of professionalism.

label: Mismatch Rate (Per Speaker)
description: Share of each speaker's segments flagged as a positive-vs-negative affect mismatch (text sentiment and detected emotion disagree), with a Global bar for the whole transcript. Taller bars mean a higher rate of mismatched segments. Mismatch flags are heuristic and do not detect sarcasm or intent.

label: Average Emotion Entropy (Per Speaker)
description: Average emotion entropy per speaker (plus a Global bar). Higher entropy means a speaker's emotion scores are spread across many categories rather than concentrated on one, indicating more mixed or ambiguous emotional expression. Lower bars indicate more emotionally focused speech.

label: Average Emotion Volatility (Per Speaker)
description: Average emotion volatility per speaker (plus a Global bar), a proxy for how often the dominant emotion changes between nearby segments. Taller bars mean more frequent shifts in primary emotion; lower bars mean steadier emotional expression.

label: Emotion Entropy Over Time
description: Emotion entropy over the course of the conversation. Higher points mark moments where emotional expression is spread across many categories rather than focused; use it to locate stretches of mixed or ambiguous affect.

label: Emotion Volatility Over Time
description: Emotion volatility over time, a proxy for how often the dominant emotion changes between nearby segments. Peaks mark stretches with rapid emotional shifts; flat low values indicate steadier affect.

label: Mismatch Flags Over Time
description: Timeline of segments flagged as a positive-vs-negative affect mismatch, drawn as a 0/1 signal over time. Spikes to 1 mark moments where text sentiment and detected emotion disagree; use it to locate divergences for review. The flag is heuristic and does not infer intent.

label: Emotion Entropy + Volatility Over Time
description: Emotion entropy and emotion volatility plotted together over time. Entropy tracks how spread-out emotional expression is; volatility tracks how often the dominant emotion changes. Read the two lines together to spot stretches of mixed and rapidly shifting affect.

label: Emotion Entropy + Volatility Over Time (Per Speaker)
description: Emotion entropy and volatility over time for a single speaker. Entropy tracks how spread-out their emotional expression is; volatility tracks how often their dominant emotion changes. One chart per speaker.

label: Mismatch Category Rates by Speaker
description: Heatmap of mismatch category rates per speaker (rows), with a Global row for the whole transcript. Columns are mismatch categories such as positive-vs-negative mismatch, trust-neutral, and high-entropy mismatch; darker cells mean that category occurs more often for that speaker. Rates are heuristic flags, not confirmed intent.

label: BERTopic Topic-Word Heatmap
description: Heatmap of word weights per BERTopic topic. Rows are topics and columns are top words; darker cells mean that word is more characteristic of that topic. Use it to interpret what each BERTopic cluster is about.

label: BERTopic Topic Prevalence
description: Share of segments assigned to each BERTopic topic, as a bar per topic. Taller bars mean that topic dominates more of the conversation. Segments with no dominant topic are excluded from the shares.
